title: ISRM cross-language result record
description: The single result shape every language runner (Julia, Rust, Python) emits after computing the InMAP ISRM tutorial from an isrm*.esm model. Comparing these files is what makes the three runners a cross-language agreement test rather than three independent scripts. Field-by-field tolerances live in compare_results.py, not here.

binding.description: Which language binding produced this record.

binding_version.description: Version/commit of the EarthSciAST binding used, for provenance.

model.description: Basename of the .esm driven, e.g. "isrm.esm". Records from different model files are comparable only if the models are numerically equivalent — isrm.esm, isrm_clean.esm and isrm_pushdown.esm all are.

mode.description: How the numbers were produced. "runtime_observed_graph": every value came from the binding's own evaluation of the .esm observed graph — the strict bar. "oracle_step0": hand-written STEP-0 arithmetic over the loader outputs, i.e. a reference oracle, NOT a demonstration that the binding executes the spec.

grid.description: Problem dimensions. Records with differing dimensions are not comparable.

n_src.description: Source cells on the SR axis (52411 at full scale).

n_rec.description: Recognized-pathway EGU FF10 emission records (43650 at full scale).

ppl.description: The emission-bearing source-cell support set — the spatial join's output. This is INTEGER-valued, so it MUST be bit-identical across bindings (CONFORMANCE_SPEC §5.5: the distinct member set is byte-identical regardless of candidate-generation backend). Any difference here is a real disagreement, never float noise.

count.description: Number of unique emission-bearing source cells (1520 at full scale).

ids.description: The full sorted 1-based source-cell id list. Optional in the file (it is `count` integers), but when present it is compared elementwise.

sha256.description: sha256 over the sorted 1-based ids serialized as decimal strings joined by "," (ASCII, no spaces, no trailing separator). Language-independent by construction.

pathways.description: Per-pathway intermediates, keyed by SR array name (SOA, pNO3, pNH4, pSO4, PrimaryPM25). Catching a disagreement here localizes it to one pathway instead of only surfacing in the death totals.

emis_sum.description: Sum of binned emissions feeding this pathway (tons/yr).

conc_sum.description: Sum over receptors of this pathway's concentration contribution, BEFORE the fact= 28766.639 scaling.

conc_max.description: Max over receptors of this pathway's concentration contribution.

total_pm25.description: The fact-scaled total PM2.5 concentration field over receptors.

deaths.description: Attributable-death fields. The tutorial targets are sum(krewski)=7524.918845602511 and sum(lepeule)=16979.632171487083.

timing.description: Non-comparable provenance: wall-clock, peak RSS, fetched bytes. Recorded for the writeup, never asserted on.

FieldSummary.description: Summary of one length-n_rcv float field. `sum` alone is a weak check (cancellation hides per-cell disagreement), so a fixed-index `sample` is required alongside it. `sha256` additionally pins bit-identity where that is expected — across bindings it is NOT expected, since float reduction order differs.

sample.description: Values at the 25 fixed 1-based indices defined by sample_indices() in compare_results.py: for k=0..24, idx_k = 1 + (k*(n_rcv-1) + 12) div 24, using INTEGER division throughout so the index set cannot drift between languages' float rounding modes. Evenly spans the grid.

sha256.description: sha256 over the full field as little-endian IEEE-754 float64 bytes. Equal ⇒ bit-identical fields. Unequal ⇒ INCONCLUSIVE, not a failure — compare `sum`/`sample` within tolerance instead. Note -0.0 and +0.0 compare equal as numbers but hash differently, so a field containing zeros can hash differently while being numerically identical.
